skill.name: gmail-tools
skill.description: Access Gmail through IMAP and SMTP using credentials stored in 1Password.
skill.summary: List, read, search, and reply to Gmail messages with 1Password-based authentication.
skill.author: ClementWalter

security_audit.summary: The skill intentionally accesses Gmail using credentials retrieved from 1Password and can read mailbox content and send replies through SMTP. Most documentation-only Markdown detections are false positives, and subprocess use calls the 1Password CLI without shell interpretation. The remaining confirmed risks are sensitive credential handling, private email access, and side-effecting email sending.

remediation.issue: Runtime scripts retrieve Gmail app passwords from 1Password.
remediation.suggestion: Document the exact credential scope, require Gmail app passwords, and avoid printing command stderr that could include sensitive details.

remediation.issue: The reply script sends email and optional attachments through SMTP.
remediation.suggestion: Require a dry-run preview or explicit user confirmation before sending messages or attaching files.

remediation.issue: Read and list commands can expose private mailbox content in terminal output.
remediation.suggestion: Warn users before displaying full message bodies and prefer limits or redaction for sensitive accounts.

content.value_statement: Email work often requires switching between tools and copying message details by hand. This skill lets Claude, Codex, and Claude Code list, read, search, and reply to Gmail using 1Password-stored credentials.
actual_capabilities: List recent messages from a Gmail folder with message IDs, senders, subjects, and dates.
Read a selected Gmail message body and basic headers by message ID.
Reply to an existing Gmail message while preserving thread headers.
Send reply attachments from local file paths when provided.
Use Gmail app passwords stored in a named 1Password item.
Accept IMAP folder names and common IMAP search query patterns.
limitations: Requires the 1Password CLI and a configured item with Gmail credentials.
Requires Gmail IMAP access and a Gmail app password, not a normal account password.
Standalone scripts cover listing, reading, and replying; advertised MCP tools may need separate server wiring.
Email sending is a real external side effect and should be previewed before use.

use_cases.title: Review incoming support messages
use_cases.description: List recent Gmail messages and read selected items before drafting a response.

use_cases.title: Reply with project attachments
use_cases.description: Send a threaded Gmail reply and include a local document as an attachment.

use_cases.title: Search mailbox context during work
use_cases.description: Use IMAP search terms to find messages from a sender or about a topic.

prompt_templates.title: List my recent Gmail messages
prompt_templates.prompt: Use gmail-tools to list the 10 most recent messages in my INBOX for the account named "Gmail Work Claude".

prompt_templates.title: Read one message
prompt_templates.scenario: Inspect a message after listing email IDs.
prompt_templates.prompt: Use gmail-tools to read message ID 46 from INBOX for the account named "Gmail Work Claude" and summarize the sender, subject, and request.

prompt_templates.title: Prepare a safe reply
prompt_templates.scenario: Draft and preview a threaded response.
prompt_templates.prompt: Use gmail-tools to prepare a dry-run reply to message ID 46 from "Gmail Work Claude". Do not send it until I approve the final text.

prompt_templates.title: Find and respond with context
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced mailbox search and reply workflow.
prompt_templates.prompt: Search INBOX for messages from sender@example.com about the contract, read the latest match, draft a concise reply, and show a dry run before sending.

output_examples.input: List the latest five Gmail messages.
output: Message IDs with sender, subject, and date are shown.
The user can choose an ID to read next.

output_examples.output: The assistant displays the sender, recipient, subject, date, and a concise summary of the message body.

output_examples.input: Reply to message 46 with an attachment after preview.
output_examples.output: The assistant shows the recipient, subject, threading headers, attachment names, and body before sending.

best_practices: Use Gmail app passwords stored in 1Password instead of normal account passwords.
Run reply actions in dry-run mode and review the recipient, subject, body, and attachments.
Limit message listing and reading to the folders and message IDs needed for the task.
anti_patterns: Do not store Gmail passwords directly in prompts, files, or shell history.
Do not send replies or attachments without reviewing a dry-run preview.
Do not use this skill on accounts where Claude should not view mailbox content.

faq.question: Does this skill require a Gmail app password?
faq.answer: Yes. The documentation says to use a Gmail app password stored in a 1Password item.

faq.question: Can it read full email bodies?
faq.answer: Yes. The read script fetches a message by ID and prints the message body and headers.

faq.question: Can it send email?
faq.answer: Yes. The reply script sends threaded Gmail replies through SMTP and can include attachments.

faq.question: Does it preserve email threads?
faq.answer: Yes. Replies use Message-ID, In-Reply-To, and References headers from the original message.

faq.question: Is the 1Password CLI required?
faq.answer: Yes. The scripts call the op command to read the named credential item.

faq.question: Should users review messages before sending?
faq.answer: Yes. Users should preview each reply, especially when attachments or external recipients are involved.
